content:
1. Scope. This standard applies to any product feature or internal tool that sends data to an AI model provider, retrieves data for a model, or acts on model output.
2. Accountability. Every AI feature has a named owner, who records its purpose and data classes before production use.
3. Provider use. Teams must send data to a provider only where the Approved Provider Schedule allows that provider for the data's class. A provider absent from the schedule is prohibited for all data.
4. Secrets. Teams must never send credentials or authentication data to a model.
5. Evaluation. Teams must run adversarial evaluations before release and after every material change.
6. Inventory. Teams must keep a current record of each model, prompt template, retrieval corpus, and tool used by a production feature.
7. Authorization. A model must not make a final authentication, authorization, or tenant-isolation decision.
8. Tools. Agents must receive only the tools their task needs, with typed inputs, and high-impact actions require approval from the feature owner.
9. Retrieval. Retrieved content is untrusted input, and retrieval must enforce the requester's permissions before content reaches a model.
10. Output. Model output is untrusted, and must be validated for its destination before it reaches a browser, query, shell, or file path.
11. Logging. Prompt and response logs inherit the highest data class they contain, and must not be kept longer than 30 days without approval from the fictional AI security owner. That approval has no 90-day limit.
12. Feedback. User feedback sent to a provider counts as data sent to that provider.
13. Accounts. Consumer accounts must not be used for non-Public data.
14. Launch. A new AI feature needs a use case record approved by the fictional AI security owner before production use.
15. Model versions. An unpinned model tag is prohibited for production use unless the gateway logs the resolved version and the change has an approved ticket.
16. Exceptions. The fictional AI security owner may approve an exception for up to 90 days. When the provider or data class is uncertain, stop and escalate to that owner.

Data classes: Public is approved for release to anyone. Internal is company data not approved for release. Restricted is customer data and regulated data.
Zephyrine Models: approved for Public and Internal data.
Quillmark AI: approved for Public data only.
Brackenfield Labs: approved for Public and Internal data.
Corvane: approved for Public data only.
Halden Systems: approved for Public and Internal data.
Merrowgate AI: approved for Public data only.
Ostlund Compute: approved for Public and Internal data.
Perrin Vale: approved for Public data only.
Sablewood: approved for Public and Internal data.
Thornquist: approved for Public data only.
No provider is approved for Restricted data. This schedule is the complete list of approved providers.
